title: Mark, again
hookLine: the first gospel you read straight through
tomorrow: why would anyone call a terrible night a gift?

lines: WHAT DOES IT SOUND LIKE NOW?
cards: Some friends tell a story without stopping for breath: and then, and right away, and then. Mark writes like that.
In the King James Bible, the little word that makes it run is straightway: "And straightway they forsook their nets, and followed him." Back in year one, this path read Mark straight through.
What does that word sound like now?

teach.b: Mark opens with no birth story, just this, in the Douay-Rheims: "The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God." Then it runs: a voice in the desert, the Jordan, the Spirit, the fishermen.
The Douay-Rheims tells the nets scene its own way: "And immediately leaving their nets, they followed him." Same speed, different English.
One to tell a friend: behind both is one small Greek word, euthys, and Mark reaches for it again and again in his first chapter. But find the still point.
After a long night of healing, Mark says: "And rising very early, going out, he went into a desert place: and there he prayed."
Even this hurried Gospel stops for that. So the line has two sides.
Straightway: still answering at once, after all these years. Still: the quiet place early, before the rush. Now the week comes back in a round.

how: Catholics hear Mark's Gospel read at Sunday Mass, especially in the year of the lectionary cycle given to Mark; some read a chapter a day or pray with a passage in the early morning.

o: the Gospel that opens with the Christmas story
the Gospel written as a book of Jesus's sayings
the Gospel in a hurry, with prayer before dawn

s: Mark's Gospel opens with the birth of Jesus
no birth story: the beginning of the gospel, then a voice in the desert.
even in fast-moving Mark 1, Jesus stops to pray before dawn
rising very early, going out, he went into a desert place: and there he prayed.

games.q: a friend you've meant to call for months texts: 'are we still friends?' what fits the fishermen in Mark 1?
o: wait for a calmer week, so the call can go well.
call her now, the way they left the nets.
send a long message explaining why you've been busy.
games.why: straightway: they left the nets and followed. some answers are better quick than perfect.

practice: Close your eyes and run Mark 1 at Mark's speed: a voice in the desert, water, a dove, nets dropped on the sand. Then slow it all the way down to before dawn: dark, quiet, one person praying alone.
Stay in that place for the rest of the time.

wordCard.voice: Mark. The Gospel in a hurry, with a still place before dawn at its center.

orig.note: Greek: straightway, at once. the small word behind Mark's speed.

carryVoice: Keep this one close: straightway, still, quick to follow and early to pray. See you next week.
